## Relevant Symbols
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:616-621` — a NEW worktree for plan/implement is made by `claude -w "$ID"` run from `$TOP`, so the session's cwd is the worktree root and cannot be an app folder. An existing worktree is entered with `cd "$WT"`. Hence: for an app-owned item the launcher creates the worktree itself (the same `git worktree add` that `--prepare` uses at `:574-579`) and starts `claude` in `$WT/<folder>` without `-w`.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:348` — `record_worktree` already turns a relative outcome `spec_dir` into `$WT/<s>` (absolute). This is where FR-010's relative storage is produced.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:551`, `:575-581`, `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh:69`, `:103` — the four readers that open `$spec_dir/...` directly; each needs the worktree-relative resolution.
- `hooks/status-board.sh:316-340` — the `rfc:` line pattern: untrusted item text, parsed by `rfc_lines`, held to a strict shape, no line → empty output exit 0. The `app:` line copies it.
- `hooks/launch-item.sh:27-38` — the RFC is read and pinned at launch from the item text whose hash the launcher already checked (`launch-item.sh:6-18`), so an `app:` line read there is the text the person registered.
- `hooks/speckit-helper.sh:268-272` — `check-specify-dir` is what `/hef.init` uses; it must stay literal to the cwd or `/hef.init` in `backend/` would see the top `.specify/` and skip.

## Existing Patterns & Conventions
- Big files get sourced siblings to stay under the code-line cap: `ledger.sh:68-71` sources `board-lib.sh`, `ledger-lanes.sh`; `session-launch.sh:51-52` sources `launch-item.sh`.
- Untrusted item lines are parsed with a strict regex and refused with the offending value quoted through `safe_name` (`status-board.sh:324,332`).
- Helpers die on stderr with the value and the expected shape, never an exit-0 sentinel (constitution 5; `speckit-helper.sh:36-39`).
- Each guard ships a mutant in its smoke part that turns the suite red (constitution 3); parts are sourced from `tests/smoke.sh:6424` (part 9 is `smoke-lane-cache.sh`).
- Byte-identity is how earlier features proved "nothing changes when unset" (`session-launch.sh:221-224`, ITEM_KIND: "a feature prompt is byte-identical to before").

## Open Questions
- None open. One rule refined from the spec: when `spec_roots` is declared and the item has no `app:` line, the
  orchestrator asks whatever the number of apps (one app plus the repository top is already two owners), and the
  launcher refuses a plan launch while `spec_root` is undecided. FR-008 is updated to say so.
- Not verifiable from code: whether Claude Code reads project `.claude/settings*.json` from the git top when it
  starts in a subfolder. Workers get their settings through `--settings` (`session-launch.sh:613`) and the
  hooks through the plugin, so the launch does not depend on it. CLAUDE.md files nest from the cwd upward, which
  is the inheritance the maintainer chose. Recorded as a risk, checked in SC-005.
